root_cause.text: The `valuesize` variable in the `wilc_scan` function of the `wilc1000` driver is declared as a `u8`, which causes an integer overflow when accumulating the total length of all probed SSIDs (up to 330 bytes) and leads to an undersized heap allocation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the type of `valuesize` in `drivers/net/wireless/microchip/wilc1000/hif.c` being changed from `u8` to `u32`. The commit description explains that the total length of up to 10 SSIDs can reach 330 bytes, which wraps around to 74 when stored in a `u8`, causing `kmalloc` to allocate an undersized buffer (75 bytes) while a subsequent `memcpy` writes up to 331 bytes.

bic_trace_step.reason: The variable `valuesize` is declared as a `u8` on line 1255. During the loop on lines 1297-1299, the lengths of the hidden network SSIDs are accumulated into `valuesize`. Because `valuesize` is an 8-bit unsigned integer, this accumulation can overflow if the total length exceeds 255. This results in an undersized heap allocation on line 1300 (`pu8HdnNtwrksWidVal = WILC_MALLOC(valuesize + 1)`), which leads to a heap buffer overflow when copying the SSID data on line 1311.
